findings.finding: The formula requires u to be injective on the whole structure but neither maps X into X nor restricts injectivity to X, so a finite X inside a larger domain can satisfy it.
findings.controlling_evidence: Dedekind infinitude of X requires an injective non-surjective self-map of X: values of arguments in X remain in X, equality of such values forces equality of the X-arguments, and at least one element of X is omitted.
findings.required_translation_handling: State all three subset-relative clauses and add an adjacent OLTESOLSET-001 disclosure.

findings.finding: The formula omits the enumerable empty set, quantifies the induction set Y over the whole domain rather than subsets of X, and closes its final bracket and parenthesis in the wrong order.
findings.controlling_evidence: The edition's enumerable-set definition includes the empty set. For nonempty X, a base point and self-map enumerate X exactly when no proper subset Y of X contains the base point and is closed under that map.
findings.required_translation_handling: Add the empty alternative, require Y to be a subset of X in the induction antecedent, balance the expression, and add an adjacent OLTESOLSET-002 disclosure.

findings.finding: The second universal clause closes the quantifier brackets without closing the conditional that begins with Y(x).
findings.controlling_evidence: The accompanying prose says that every x in Y codes a subset of X, which is the complete conditional Y(x) implies the universal coding condition.
findings.required_translation_handling: Close the outer conditional before the x-quantifier bracket and add an adjacent OLTESOLSET-003 disclosure.

source.locator: lines 113-120, proof that Cont(Y) expresses continuum size

findings.finding: The proof says the coding association targets subsets of s(Z), although Z is only a bound variable and X is the base set whose power set is coded.
findings.controlling_evidence: Both Pow(Y,R,X) and the preceding sentences consistently identify s(X) as the base set and its subsets as the coded objects.
findings.required_translation_handling: Replace s(Z) by s(X) in the proof explanation and add an adjacent OLTESOLSET-004 disclosure.

source.locator: lines 123-129, characterization of a continuum-sized domain

findings.finding: The proposed witness u is injective and every element of Y is in its range, but the formula never requires the range of u to lie in Y; the identity function therefore satisfies the weak clauses for arbitrary Y.
findings.controlling_evidence: Equality between the domain cardinality and the continuum-coded set Y requires a bijection from the entire domain onto Y, so every u(x) must belong to Y in addition to injectivity and surjectivity onto Y.
findings.required_translation_handling: Add the missing universal range-in-Y clause and an adjacent OLTESOLSET-005 disclosure.

findings.finding: The formula requires u to be injective on the entire structure domain. Equinumerous subsets X and Y can have complements of different sizes, so a bijection from X onto Y need not extend to an injective total endofunction of the domain.
findings.controlling_evidence: A bijection from X onto Y requires range containment for arguments in X, injectivity only between arguments in X, and surjectivity from X onto Y; values on elements outside X are irrelevant.
findings.required_translation_handling: Restrict the injectivity antecedent to X(x) and X(y), and add an adjacent OLTESOLSET-006 disclosure.

findings.finding: The universal condition includes Y = X, which forces any satisfying X to be finite or of size aleph-zero, while the final conjunct excludes the latter; consequently finite sets satisfy the formula and an aleph-one-sized set does not.
findings.controlling_evidence: A set has size aleph-one exactly when it is infinite and not of size aleph-zero while every proper subset is finite or of size aleph-zero.
findings.required_translation_handling: Restrict the universal condition to proper subsets, add infinitude of X, and add an adjacent OLTESOLSET-007 disclosure.
